To prove the theorem `lg_target`, we need to show that the Killing form restricted to the range of the adjoint representation `LieDerivation.ad R L` is nondegenerate, which implies it is a Killing form.

The key idea is to use the fact that the Killing form is nondegenerate when the Lie algebra is semisimple (which follows from being Killing). Since the adjoint representation maps into the Lie algebra of derivations, and the range of the adjoint map is a subalgebra, we can use properties of Killing forms and their restriction to subspaces.

In particular, if the Killing form is nondegenerate on the entire Lie algebra, then its restriction to any subspace with trivial radical (i.e., no nontrivial elements annihilated by the form) will also be nondegenerate. In this case, the range of the adjoint map is known to have a trivial radical under certain finiteness and killing conditions.

Thus, we can apply existing lemmas in Mathlib that relate the nondegeneracy of the Killing form to the structure of the Lie algebra and its subalgebras, especially those involving finite modules and Killing forms. This allows us to conclude that the Killing form restricted to the range of the adjoint map is nondegenerate, hence it is a Killing form on that subspace.
